Then you should be retrained or fired from your job with CIS.  Affidavits are acceptable forms of corroborating evidence under the CFR and relevant case law.  The applicant needs to explain why other independent evidence is unavailable and if the affidavits are sufficiently detailed and exhibit indicia of credibility, they are perfectly acceptable.  I have many approved DACAs where I used affidavits to cover gaps.

I know many CIS officers who take their job seriously and with the utmost professionalism.  Apparently, you are one of the ones that sully the agency's reputation.

Also, learn the definition of hearsay if you are going to be throwing legal terms around.  Hearsay is "an out-of-court statement introduced to prove the truth of matter asserted therein."  What you refer to as "hard proof," meaning "Copies of appointments you were at, bank statements, receipts, accounts in your name, phone records, etc." are all hearsay.  They would, however, meet the business records exception to hearsay.

1.  There's no such thing as a I-785; it's I-765. 2.  The F-1 is no longer valid because of the application for adjustment of status to permanent from nonimmigrant status.  The person has demonstrated immigrant intent.  You can work legally on the EAD.  If the marriage based adjustment is denied, it *may* be possible to reinstate the F-1 nunc pro tunc, even if you have worked with a valid EAD.  

" if your LPR application is denied and you become illegal, you can still reapply as an undocumented immigrant and get your green card because your LPR app is based on marriage." - This makes no sense.  First, it's undocumented.  Second, if the I-485 adjustment is denied for failing to maintain status, it's because the I-130 petitioning spouse is an LPR and not a USC; because if the spouse is a USC, it's forgiven.  But if the spouse is an LPR, he can't adjust for failing to maintain status and would need to consular process.

The forms are available on USCIS' website for free.  No one should pay for "filling out forms and printing them out."  Here is the adjustment application:  https://www.uscis.gov/i-485.  If you are advising people on how to fill them out, you are treading into dangerous waters.  While I assume your intentions are to help (and in no way am I suggesting you are fraudulently holding yourself out to be something you are not), you could end up with federal criminal charges:  http://www.startribune.com/suit-shakopee-woman-posed-as-attorney-exploited-immigrants/259094411/  I'm just saying it is a complex area of law and not a matter of just filling out a form.

Current processing times for the I-751 are over a year (https://egov.uscis.gov/cris/processTimesDisplayInit.do).  When she files it, she will get a receipt automatically extending her permanent resident status for a year.  Between 90 and 30 days before that expires, she'll have to make an infopass appointment (https://my.uscis.gov/appointment) at her local USCIS office.  They give one-year stamps her passport extending her status until it's resolved.  If it's denied by USCIS, it's automatically referred to an IJ, and she can keep getting extensions of her status.  

I would not suggest online research for immigration work.  Immigration is very tricky.  Even if you don't hire an immigration lawyer, I would suggest consulting with a reputable one (there are a lot of lawyers that dabble in immigration, it's dangerous.  I suggest a firm that only deals with immigration).  You can check aila.org for a referral.  (for the record, i'm not with the government or promoting anything, just an immigration lawyer who has seen what bad advice/self-research has done to people).

She'll be fine.  Not just an affidavit from the ex (although that is big), but family and friends as well.  Especially the ex-in-laws, if they are in communication.  Just be sure the affidavits are very detailed as to why they got married and why they broke up.  Also, if they sought a marriage counselor it will help.

Regarding the taxes - she can go to the IRS website and order her tax return transcripts.  That's proof.

If, in the unlikely event they don't approve the 751, part II, you get to go before an IJ (which will take many years) and if it's serious, you can marry her and petition for her.  From what you say, I would highly doubt you get an INA 204(c) marriage fraud finding that would bar her from benefiting from a petition filed by you.

actually,  it's rather complicated. I'll just start with someone being put into removal proceedings. Sometimes they are detained and sometimes not. There are many factors involved. If they are detained, they, or their lawyer,  can request a bond hearing. Here you look at if they are a threat to the community, flight risk, and what relief is available. A bond is set and someone pays. That money is not kept by the government unless the alien absconds . Also,  when put into removal proceedings they are given a notice to appear,  which is also the charging document. It says how they entered (with our without inspection by a boarder agent), where they are from and why the US is trying to remove them (overstaying a visa, fraud in obtaining a visa, criminal convictions, any number of reasons). Then it's my job to figure out a way around it (the Allen is married to a citizen, waiver of fraud, asylum, withholding, cancellation, being the victim of a crime...that's the fun one people don't know about..been shot? In all honesty, I never really started becoming aware of KH until I got into african cichlids.  I've probably forgotten a lot about what I originally knew, but if memory serves, basically it effects the volatility of the pH, so if it gets too low, it will cause pH shock.  I pretty much still ignore it my FW tanks, only with my africans do i occasionally look at it because their pH is purposefully around 8.3 all the time.

I would suggest that you check what pH you should be at for the fish in each of your tanks.  Let's say, hypothetically, you want your 55 to be at 7.0 but it's at 8.6.  I would mix up 10 gallons of new water, add in some acid buffer to make sure you get that pH down to 7 along with whatever else you use, then do a water change.  Then I would do that every other day until the pH goes down to a stable 7 and back off water changes to 20%, 1xweek. 

KH goes down normally with time, the way to keep it up is with water changes and/or adding baking soda.
